Definition: probably from G4524; a Sadducæan (i.e. Tsadokian), or follower of a certain heretical Israelite:--Sadducee.
BiblicalUsage: Saddoukaîos names a Sadducæan (that is Tsadokian), or follower of a certain heretical Israelite. In Acts 4:1, we read, "…unto the people, the priests, and the captain…"; in Luke 20:27, "…certain of the Sadducees, which deny that there…". You hear it again in Mark 12:18 — "…the Sadducees, which say there is no resurrection…" — and in Matthew 3:7, "…them, O generation of vipers, who hath warned…".
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that Saddoukaîos is no accident in the text, and it names something real, and God does not use empty words. And I hold that Saddoukaîos is as true now as when it was first written, because God does not change.
